name: Trap evals (LLM, operator-run)
cadence: on demand (via an operator at the shell; no cron line)

knobs.note: no static default — the script computes it ($SELF/agent-call.sh). Read by bin/trap-eval.sh as ${TRAP_EVAL_AGENT_CALL:-$SELF/agent-call.sh}. NOT settable from the control plane — it is the command every cell runs, a test seam, so only env/global.env on the box moves it.

Read by bin/trap-eval.sh as ${TRAP_EVAL_FIXTURES:-}; empty falls through to the deployed harness, the checkout, then the script's own tree. NOT settable from the control plane — it is a path a root lane reads scenarios and judges from, so only env/global.env on the box moves it.
Seconds one scenario's judge.sh may run (timeout(1)) before its verdict is null. Read by bin/trap-eval.sh as ${TRAP_EVAL_JUDGE_TIMEOUT:-300}.

0 makes this lane call no model at all. bin/lib/llm-gate.sh refuses BEFORE the vendor call and writes a zero-cost row_source=refused row, so the stop is visible in the ledger rather than being a lane that went quiet.

Comma/space list of the ONLY ladder rungs this lane may reach. Empty is every rung, i.e. today's ladder unchanged. A rung outside the list is refused before the call, so a cliff or a failure on the standing lane cannot descend into one that costs ~100x (#1141, the $793 descent).

Dollars this lane may spend in the current UTC day, summed from D1 cost_rows through GET /api/metrics/llm-spend — never from the box's own logs/cost.csv. A second, project-scoped ceiling is the lane.<id>.<project>.llm_usd_cap_day row, which is read only when somebody wrote it.
